observable: minimum flexible (G4S)-type linker length for intramolecular VH-VL pairing (a monomeric scFv); shorter linkers force diabodies
note: VH C-terminus to VL N-terminus gap in an Fv is ~35 A. Linkers >=~12 res give monomeric scFv; <=~10 force diabodies. Tests the 3.5 A/res extended-coil reach bound. The model lower bound (fully extended) underestimates the empirical threshold slightly because real coils are not fully extended.

observable: a 5-residue linker cannot bridge VH and VL on the same chain so the Fv pairs across chains (diabody / dimer)
note: Maximum extended-coil reach 3.5x5 = 17.5 A is well under the ~35 A VH-VL gap -> predicted cannot span -> observed diabody.

observable: a 15-residue (G4S)3 linker bridges VH-VL intramolecularly so the chain folds as a monomeric scFv
note: Maximum extended-coil reach 3.5x15 = 52.5 A exceeds the ~35 A gap -> predicted can span -> observed monomeric scFv.

observable: inter-fluorophore distance increases ~linearly with (EAAAK)n length (behaves as a rigid alpha-helix rod)
note: Helix modelled as a rigid rod with ~1.5 A/res axial rise; longer helix -> larger controllable separation. NB this dataset is the source of the 1.5 A/res constant so the per-residue value is a consistency check; the directional length->distance coupling is the claim being validated.

observable: inter-fluorophore distance is only weakly dependent on (GGGGS)n length (flexible coil collapses to a broad distance distribution)

observable: which linker holds the two fluorophore domains at a more fixed separation
note: Tests the library premise helix=rigid / coil=flexible against a real construct. EAAAK gives a length-tunable fixed distance while GS collapses -> the rigid one is the helix.
